messages:
mia (product): Quick sync: draft proposal for Reserved Capacity pacing + fallback behavior for EU Dedicated customers. Aim: keep committed throughput predictable, avoid runaway token usage, and provide clear opt-in for cross-region failover. Looking for engineering constraints and launch criteria.

raj (eng-sre): High level sounds good. Two immediate asks: 1) define the pacing cadence (minute vs hour granularity); 2) define observable states (ok/warning/critical) and the exact decision triggers for fallback. Also: simulate in load tests.

jules (eng-platform): Implementation idea: per-tenant sliding-minute budget aggregated into 1h rolling window. States: green <=70%, yellow 70-90%, red >90% (on rolling 1h). Transitions: if state moves to red for 2 consecutive 5m windows, trigger fallback policy.

lina (eng-runtime): Runtime notes: we have model-variant routing primitives and token counters. To avoid stamping KV hot keys, we'll shard tenant counters and use approximate counting (reservoir sketch) for high-QPS tenants. Routing policy snippet: ``rule: if tenant_state == red and local_variant_available -> route: local-quant; elif tenant_state == red and cross_region_opt_in -> route: eu-west; else -> reject/soft-throttle``.

sam (sales): Customers expect a visible threshold so they can opt to buy extra capacity rather than be routed. We should expose "remaining hourly budget" and an "emergency burst" purchase option in console. Also need templated wording for customer notifications when we throttle or fallback.

mia (product): Agreed on UI. For regulated EU customers default should be: no cross-region fallback unless explicit opt-in. Non-regulated customers can have opt-out instead. We need consent audit logs.

legal-bot: Reminder: cross-border routing for data subject requests may require DSAR handling. Add privacy review before enabling cross-region for any tenant.

raj (eng-sre): Ops safety: circuit-breaker criteria proposal: sustained 5m p95 latency increase > 150ms OR error rate delta > 0.8% triggers auto-revert of routing decisions and pages SRE. Add a cooldown of 10m after revert.

ops-oncall: I'll write the runbook steps: how to flip global kill-switch, how to set per-tenant opt-in, how to drain a fallback variant back to primary. Need API endpoints and console buttons documented.

jules (eng-platform): Telemetry we need: tenant_id, tenant_bucket_state, decision, fallback_variant, decision_reason, trigger_window, pre_fallback_metrics (p95, errors). Retention: 60d for billing/regression, sample full traces on 1% of fallbacks.

lina (eng-runtime): Engineering constraints: pushing per-tenant policy updates to thousands of tenants should be batched. We'll canary the policy push to a small set of internal tenants (5) then to 2% of production Dedicated tenants. Also need feature-flag canary for the UI opt-in flow.

mia (product): Draft launch criteria: 1) policy engine + per-tenant buckets live in staging; 2) runtime routing + local-quantized and smaller-variant fallbacks validated; 3) console opt-in UI with consent audit logs; 4) telemetry + alerting wired; 5) legal privacy signoff for cross-region opt-in. Soft launch to 10% dedicated EU customers after canaries pass.

sam (sales): We should surface a "fallback SLA" in the contract addendum so customers know latency/quality tradeoffs if they opt into cross-region. Sales will prepare 3 customer-facing templates.

raj (eng-sre): Pre-deploy tests: simulate 2x reserved capacity burst with mixed fallbacks to make sure we don't cascade (no amplification), verify KV shards hold under load, and ensure rollback path completes in <3 minutes.

jules (eng-platform): For rollout controls: expose these toggles: feature_flag.pacing_v1 (boolean), rollout_slice_percentage (int), cross_region_opt_in (per-tenant boolean). Default: pacing_v1=false. Our push plan: internal canary -> 2% -> 10% -> 100%.

mia (product): Owners and next steps: jules + lina to write API/policy spec (ETA EOD today), raj to draft staging load tests, ops-oncall to draft runbook snippets, sam to draft customer messages and contract language, legal-bot to coordinate privacy review. Sync tomorrow 10:30am.

ops-oncall: One more ask: add an automated customer notification channel (console + email + webhooks) when tenant enters yellow or red state. That reduces surprise support tickets.

mia (product): Good call. We'll include notification hooks in the spec. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
